rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dhāriyāt are the winds, which scatter dust and other things.
rows.anchor: الرياح لأنها تذور التراب وغيره

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: A reading assimilates the tāʾ into the dhāl.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بإدغام التاء في الذال { فالحاملات وقرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden bearers are clouds, because they carry rain.
rows.anchor: { فالحاملات وقرا } السحاب ، لأنها تحمل المطر

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: A reading vocalizes waqran with fatḥa on the wāw, naming the carried load by its verbal noun or substituting it for ḥamlan.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وقرا ) بفتح الواو على تسمية المحمول بالمصدر . أو على إيقاعه موقع حملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The things running are ships.
rows.anchor: { فالجاريات يسرا } الفلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusran means running with ease, that is, easy running.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ( يسرا ) : جريا ذا يسر ، أي ذا سهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distributors are angels, dividing matters such as rain and provisions under command.
rows.anchor: الملائكة ، لأنها تقسم الأمور من الأمطار والأرزاق وغيرها . وتفعل التقسيم مأمورة بذلك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the angels divide human affairs: Gabriel handles severity, Michael mercy, the death angel takes souls, and Israfil blows the trumpet.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : تتولى تقسيم أمر العباد : جبريل للغلظة ، وميكائيل للرحمة . وملك الموت لقبض الأرواح ، وإسرافيل للنفخ

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: In a pulpit exchange with Ibn al-Kawwa, Ali identified the oath figures respectively as winds, clouds, ships, and angels.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال وهو على المنبر : سلوني قبل أن لا تسألوني ، ولن تسألوا بعدي مثلي ، فقام ابن الكواء فقال : ما الذريات ذروا ؟ قال : الرياح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to give the same identifications of the four oath figures.
rows.anchor: فالمقسمات أمرا ؟ قال : الملائكة وكذا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan identifies the distributors as clouds, through which God apportions provisions to His servants.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ( المقسمات ) السحاب ، يقسم الله بها أرزاق العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distributors have also been interpreted as the seven planets.
rows.anchor: وقد حملت على الكواكب السبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading takes all four oath descriptions as winds: they form and carry clouds, move them through the air, and distribute rain by directing them.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد : الرياح لا غير ؛ لأنها تنشىء السحاب وتقله وتصرفه ، وتجري في الجو جريا سهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first interpretation, the fāʾs order the winds, the clouds they drive, ships moved by their blowing, and angels apportioning provisions through rain and sea trade.
rows.anchor: فبالسحاب الذي تسوقه ، فبالفلك التي تجريها بهبوبها ، فبالملائكة التي تقسم الأرزاق بإذن الله من الأمطار وتجارات البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the wind-only reading, the sequence follows the winds' actions: they blow, scatter dust and gravel, move clouds, spread them in the air, and apportion rain.
rows.anchor: لأنها تنشىء السحاب وتقله وتصرفه ، وتجري في الجو جريا سهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “whatever you are promised” answers the oath; mā can be relative or a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم ، وما موصولة أو مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is promised is resurrection.
rows.anchor: والموعود : البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A true promise” uses an adjectival construction like “a pleasing life.”
rows.anchor: ووعد صادق : كعيشة راضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dīn here means recompense.
rows.anchor: والدين : الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wāqiʿ means that which comes to pass.
rows.anchor: والواقع : الحاصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Likewise” means “in the same way”; it points to the deniers' rejection of the Messenger and calling him a magician and madman.
rows.anchor: الأمر ، أي مثل ذلك ، وذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf cannot be accusative governed by atā, because the negative mā prevents what follows it from governing an earlier word; “lam yaʾti” would work.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح أن تكون الكاف منصوبة بأتى ؛ لأن ما النافية لا يعمل ما بعدها فيما قبلها . ولو قيل : لم يأت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “did they enjoin it on one another?” refers to the shared saying; the question imagines earlier and later peoples agreeing on it.
rows.anchor: الضمير للقول ، يعنى : أتواصى الأولون والآخرون بهذا القول حتى قالوه جميعا متفقين عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not meet in one time to coordinate; their common cause was transgression, which drove them to the same accusation.
rows.anchor: لم يتلاقوا في زمان واحد ، بل جمعتهم العلة الواحدة وهي الطغيان ، والطغيان هو الحامل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am is disconnected, and its hamza signals denial: a person does not get whatever he wishes.
rows.anchor: هي أم المنقطعة ومعنى الهمزة فيها الإنكار ، أي : ليس للإنسان ما تمنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended wish is their hope that their idols would intercede, an extremely remote presumption upon God.
rows.anchor: والمراد طمعهم في شفاعة الآلهة ، وهو تمن على الله في غاية البعد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes the wish as their claim that, if returned to their Lord, they would receive the best.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو قولهم : { ولئن رجعت إلى ربى إن لى عنده للحسنى }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra's boast that he would be given wealth and children.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو قول الوليد بن المغيرة ( لأوتين مالا وولدا )

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reported interpretation is that some wished to be the Prophet himself.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو تمنى بعضهم أن يكون هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns both the hereafter and this world, giving or withholding from either as He wills; no one can dictate anything to Him.
rows.anchor: أي هو مالكهما ، فهو يعطي منهما من يشاء ويمنع من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean ruin and fires, or misguidance from truth in this world and fires in the next.
rows.anchor: في هلاك ونيران . أو في ضلال عن الحق في الدنيا ، ونيران في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being touched by Saqar describes the fire's heat and painful licking, as one speaks of feeling fever's touch or tasting a beating.
rows.anchor: لأن النار إذا أصابتهم بحرهاولفحتهم بإيلامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative “taste” presupposes the omitted phrase “it was said.”
rows.anchor: وذوقوا : على إرادة القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar is a proper name for Hell, derived from a verb meaning that fire scorched or burned someone.
rows.anchor: وسقر : علم لجهنم . من سقرته النار وصقرته إذا لوحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses ṣaqara for the sun's scorching heat.
rows.anchor: قال ذو الرمة : إذا ذابت الشمس اتقى صقراتها … بأفنان مربوع الصريمة معبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar is diptote because it is both a proper name and feminine.
rows.anchor: وعدم صرفها للتعريف والتأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kulla shayʾin is accusative under an omitted verb explained by the following verb; a reading instead has nominative kulla shayʾin.
rows.anchor: منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره الظاهر

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: Both vocalizations, al-qadar and al-qadr, are read; both mean determination or measuring.
rows.anchor: التقدير . وقرىء بهما ، أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that each thing was created measured, wise, and ordered according to what wisdom required.
rows.anchor: أي : خلقنا كل شيء مقدرا محكما مرتبا على حسب ما اقتضته الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that each thing was measured and written in the Preserved Tablet, with its state and time known before it existed.
rows.anchor: أو مقدرا مكتوبا في اللوح . معلوما قبل كونه ، قد علمنا حاله وزمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command is one swift word of bringing something into being: when He wills it, it comes to be without delay.
rows.anchor: إلا كلمة واحدة سريعة التكوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jawār are ships.
rows.anchor: الجوار } السفن . وقرىء

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: A reading drops the yāʾ and leaves the rāʾ nominative, as in the cited line whose word “ثمان” illustrates the form.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( الجوار ) بحذف الياء ورفع الراء ، ونحوه : لها ثنايا أربع حسان … وأربع فكلها ثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munshaʾāt are ships with raised sails; with kasra on the shīn, it can mean ships raising sails or making waves as they move.
rows.anchor: المرفوعات الشرع . وقرىء : بكسر الشين : وهي الرافعات الشرع أو اللاتي ينشئن الأمواج بجريهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-aʿlām is the plural of ʿalam, a tall mountain.
rows.anchor: والأعلام : جمع علم ، وهو الجبل الطويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These two gardens lie below the pair promised to those brought near, and are for the companions of the right, who rank below them.
rows.anchor: ومن دون تينك الجنتين الموعودتين للمقربين { جنتان } لمن دونهم من أصحاب اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mudhāmmatān means the gardens are intensely green.
rows.anchor: قد ادهامتا من شدة الخضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naḍḍākhātān means gushing with water; nadhkh is stronger than nadh, which is like sprinkling.
rows.anchor: فوارتان بالماء . والنضخ أكثر من النضح ، لأن النضح غير معجمة مثل الرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Palm and pomegranate are singled out from fruit to show their distinction and merit, as though their excellence made them separate kinds.
rows.anchor: اختصاصا لهما وبيانا لفضلهما ، كأنهما لما لهما من المزية جنسان آخران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, dates are both fruit and food, while pomegranates are fruit and medicine, so neither is exclusively for enjoyment.
rows.anchor: أو لأن النخل ثمره فاكهة وطعام ، والرمان فاكهة ودواء ، فلم يخلصا للتفكه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa rules that one who swears not to eat fruit does not break the oath by eating pomegranate or fresh dates; his two companions disagree.
rows.anchor: ومنه قال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله : إذا حلف لا يأكل فاكهة فأكل رمانا أو رطبا : لم يحنث ، وخالفه صاحباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tūrūna means striking fire and drawing it from firesticks; Arabs rub two sticks, calling the upper one the male and the lower one the female, by analogy with mating cattle.
rows.anchor: تقدحونها وتستخرجونها من الزناد والعرب تقدح بعودين تحك أحدهما على الآخر ، ويسمون الأعلى : الزند ، والأسفل : الزندة ؛ شبهوهما بالفحل والطروقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree is the one from which the firesticks are made.
rows.anchor: التي منها الزناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is a reminder of Hell because ordinary livelihood depends on fire, keeping it constantly before people as a sign of the threatened punishment.
rows.anchor: تذكيرا لنار جهنهم ، حيث علقنا بها أسباب المعايش كلها ، وعممنا بالحاجة إليها البلوى لتكون حاضرة للناس ينظرون إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the fire is a reminder and model of Hell.
rows.anchor: أو جعلناها تذكرة وأنموذجا من جهنم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says the fire people kindle is one seventieth of Hell's heat; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿan means benefit or use.
rows.anchor: ومتاعا } ومنفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muqwīn can mean people who lodge in barren country, or people whose bellies or provisions are empty; aqwaytu can mean going days without food.
rows.anchor: للذين ينزلون القواء وهي القفر . أو للذين خلت بطونهم أو مزاودهم من الطعام . يقال : أقويت من أيام ، أي لم آكل شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may mean begin glorifying by uttering God's name, or “name” may mean remembrance, so glorify by remembering your Lord.
rows.anchor: فأحدث التسبيح بذكر اسم ربك ، أو أراد بالاسم : الذكر ، أي : بذكر ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿaẓīm can grammatically modify either the annexed noun or its genitive complement.
rows.anchor: صفة للمضاف أو للمضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the signs of God's power and favor, glorify Him by saying subḥān Allāh: to reject deniers' claims, marvel at their ingratitude, or thank Him for the listed blessings.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر ما دل على قدرته وإنعامه على عباده قال : فأحدث التسبيح وهو أن يقول : سبحان الله ، إما تنزيها له عما يقول الظالمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For the poor” is apposition to “those of kin” and its conjunct; it cannot be apposed to God, the Messenger, and their conjuncts.
rows.anchor: للفقراء } بدل من قوله : { ذا القربى } والمعطوف عليه والذي منع الإبدال من : لله وللرسول والمعطوف عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is excluded from being called poor in the apposition because God distinguishes His Messenger from the poor, and the surface construction would violate reverence due to God.
rows.anchor: أن الله عز وجل أخرج رسوله من الفقراء في قوله : { وينصرون الله ورسوله } وأنه يترفع برسول الله عن التسمية بالفقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those are the truthful” means truthful in their faith and struggle.
rows.anchor: { أولئك هم الصادقون } في إيمانهم وجهادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who settled the abode are the Anṣār, and the phrase is coordinated with the Muhājirūn.
rows.anchor: معطوف على المهاجرين ، وهم الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordination of faith with the abode can mean they settled the city and sincerely embraced faith, as in the cited coordination of unlike objects.
rows.anchor: معناه تبوؤا الدار وأخلصوا الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they made faith a settled home because they were firmly rooted and steadfast in it, just as they settled in the city.
rows.anchor: وجعلوا الإيمان مستقرا ومتوطنا لهم لتمكنهم منه واستقامتهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “the abode” means the abode of migration and faith: the definite article stands for a possessive construction, with “abode” elided from “abode of faith.”
rows.anchor: أراد دار الهجرة ودار الإيمان ، فأقام لام التعريف في الدار مقام المضاف إليه ، وحذف المضاف من دار الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Medina itself is called faith because it is the abode of migration and the place where faith appeared.
rows.anchor: أو سمى المدينة لأنها دار الهجرة ومكان ظهور الإيمان بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Before them” means before the Muhājirūn, because the Anṣār settled the abode of migration and faith first; another view takes it as before their migration.
rows.anchor: من قبل المهاجرين ؛ لأنهم سبقوهم في تبوىء دار الهجرة والإيمان . وقيل : من قبل هجرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā yajidūn means they do not find or know within themselves; ḥājah is a desired need for any of the spoils given to the migrants, and their hearts do not covet it.
rows.anchor: ولا يعلمون في أنفسهم { حاجة مما أوتوا } أي طلب محتاج إليه مما أوتي المهاجرون من الفيء وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A needed thing is called a ḥājah, as in telling someone to take his need or giving him the amount he needs.
rows.anchor: والمحتاج إليه يسمى حاجة ؛ يقال : خذ منه حاجتك ، وأعطاه من ماله حاجته

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet distributed Banū Naḍīr's property among the Muhājirūn, except for three needy Anṣār; he offered the Anṣār a choice, and they chose to share homes and property and prefer the migrants in the spoils.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قسم أموال بني النضير على المهاجرين ولم يعط الأنصار إلا ثلاثة نفر محتاجين : أبادجانة سماك بن خرشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṣāṣah means need or poverty, originally referring to gaps in a house; the clause is circumstantial, assuming their poverty.
rows.anchor: أي خلة ، وأصلها : خصاص البيت ، وهي فروجه ؛ والجملة في موضع الحال ، أي : مفروضة خصاصتهم

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: Shuḥḥ is read with either ḍamma or kasra on the shīn.
rows.anchor: بالضم والكسر ، وقد قرىء بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuḥḥ is meanness: a soul's tight, greedy resistance to giving, as illustrated by the cited line.
rows.anchor: اللؤم ، وأن تكون نفس الرجل كزة حريصة على المنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain passage is an imaginative analogy, as in the parable of the trust; it rebukes people for hard hearts and lack of humility when reciting and pondering the Qurʾān's warnings.
rows.anchor: هذا تمثيل وتخييل ، كما مر في قوله تعالى : ( إنا عرضنا الأمانة )

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: A reading has muṣṣaddiʿan through assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( مصدعا ) على الإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those parables” refers to this analogy and other parables elsewhere in revelation.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى هذا المثل وإلى أمثاله في مواضع من التنزيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghayb can mean the nonexistent and al-shahādah the existing and perceptible; alternatives are what servants do not or do witness, secrecy and openness, or this world and the next.
rows.anchor: المعدوم { والشهادة } الموجود المدرك كأنه يشاهده . وقيل : ما غاب عن العباد وما شاهدوه . وقيل : السر والعلانية . وقيل : الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: Al-quddūs is read with either ḍamma or fatḥa on the qāf.
rows.anchor: بالضم والفتح وقد قرىء بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-quddūs means exceedingly pure from anything reprehensible, like al-subūḥ, a word used in angels' glorification.
rows.anchor: البليغ في النزاهة عما يستقبح . ونظيره : السبوح ، وفي تسبيح الملائكة : سبوح قدوس رب الملائكة والروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-salām means safety; as an attribute it either emphatically declares God free of defects or means that He grants safety.
rows.anchor: بمعنى السلامة . ومنه { دار السلام }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muʾmin means the giver of security.
rows.anchor: المؤمن ) واهب الأمن . وقرىء بفتح الميم

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: With fatḥa on the mīm, al-muʾman means “the one believed in,” with the preposition omitted, as in the description of Moses' chosen people.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بفتح الميم بمعنى المؤمن به على حذف الجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muhaymin is the watcher over everything and its guardian; its form is derived from amn with the hamza changed to hāʾ.
rows.anchor: الرقيب على كل شيء ، الحافظ له ، مفيعل من الأمن ؛ إلا أن همزته قلبت هاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jabbār is the overpowering one who compels creation to what He wills.
rows.anchor: القاهر الذي جبر خلقه على ما أراد ، أي أجبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mutakabbir means surpassing in majesty and greatness, or transcendent above wronging His servants.
rows.anchor: البليغ الكبرياء والعظمة . وقيل : المتكبر عن ظلم عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khāliq is the one who determines what He brings into existence.
rows.anchor: المقدر لما يوجده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-bāriʾ distinguishes created things from one another through their different forms.
rows.anchor: المميز بعضه من بعض بالأشكال المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muṣawwir is the one who gives form.
rows.anchor: و { المصور } الممثل . وعن حاطب

rows.speaker: حاطب بن أبي بلتعة
rows.claim: Ḥāṭib reads al-bāriʾ al-muṣawwir with fatḥa on the wāw and accusative rāʾ, meaning the one who creates the form-giver and differentiates what it forms by varied shapes.
rows.anchor: وعن حاطب بن أبي بلتعة أنه قرأ : ( البارىء المصور ) ، بفتح الواو ونصب الراء

words: يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads “and whatever is in the earth,” omitting the reference to the heavens.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : ( وما في الأرض )

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports asking the Prophet about God's greatest name; the Prophet tells him to read the end of al-Hashr often, repeating the answer when asked again.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says whoever recites Sūrat al-Hashr will have earlier and later sins forgiven; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We carried you” means God carried the ancestors of the present audience in the ship; their survival was a favor to descendants, who are as though they themselves were carried.
rows.anchor: حملنا آباءكم { فى الجارية } في سفينة ؛ لأنهم إذا كانوا من نسل المحمولين الناجين ، كان حمل آبائهم منة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jāriyah here means a ship.
rows.anchor: { فى الجارية } في سفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the event: believers being saved and disbelievers drowned, made a moral lesson.
rows.anchor: الضمير للفعلة : وهي نجاة المؤمنين وإغراق الكفرة { تذكرة } عظة وعبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An attentive ear retains and remembers what it hears and does not waste it by failing to act; what is kept inside is waʿayta, what is stored outside awʿayta.
rows.anchor: من شأنها أن تعي وتحفظ ما سمعت به ولا تضيعه بترك العمل ، وكل ما حفظته في نفسك فقد وعيته وما حفظته في غير نفسك فقد أوعيته

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: At the verse's revelation, the Prophet asked God to make it Ali's ear; Ali says afterward he never forgot anything and had no right to forget.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular indefinite “ear” signals that attentive listeners are few, rebukes the many who fail to heed, and says one ear that understands God counts as the great majority before Him.
rows.anchor: للإيذان بأن الوعاة فيهم قلة ، ولتوبيخ الناس بقلة من يعي منهم ؛ وللدلالة على أن الأذن الواحدة إذا وعت وعقلت عن الله فهي السواد الأعظم عند الله

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: A reading has sukūn on the ʿayn in wa-taʿīhā to lighten the pronunciation, likened to kabid.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وتعيها ) بسكون العين للتخفيف : شبه تعي بكبد

none: The segment contains only the quoted verse.

words: إِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ سَبْحًۭا طَوِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabḥan with sīn means activity and movement among tasks and needs, leaving the night free for intimate converse with God, which requires an unoccupied mind.
rows.anchor: تصرفا وتقلبا في مهماتك وشواغلك ، ولا تفرغ إلا بالليل ؛ فعليك بمناجاة الله التي تقتض فراغ البال وانتفاء الشواغل

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: A reading with khāʾ instead of sīn is a metaphor from teasing apart wool fibers, like the scattering of concern and the heart through distractions.
rows.anchor: وأما القراءة بالخاء فاستعارة من سبخ الصوف ، وهو نفشه ونشر أجزائه ؛ لانتشار الهم وتفرق القلب بالشواغل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is more conducive to inner agreement and recitation because people are calm and quiet; it gathers the heart and concerns, unlike daytime distractions.
rows.anchor: وهو أن الليل أعون على المواطأة وأشد للقراءة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes sabḥan as free time and spaciousness for sleep and tending to one's needs.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فراغا وسعة لنومك وتصرفك في حوائجك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says missed night prayer can be made up in free time during the day.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن فاتك من الليل شيء فلك في النهار فراغ تقدر على تداركه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God continually by night and day and pursue every good form of remembrance: glorification, declarations of unity and greatness, prayer, Qurʾān recitation, study, and more; the Messenger filled his time with it.
rows.anchor: ودم على ذكره في ليلك ونهارك ، واحرص عليه ، وذكر الله يتناول كل ما كان من ذكر طيب : تسبيح ، وتهليل ، وتكبير ، وتمجيد ، وتوحيد ، وصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabattal ilayhi means detach yourself and devote yourself to God.
rows.anchor: وتبتل إليه } وانقطع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabtīlan stands where tabattulan might be expected because tabattala means “detach oneself”; the wording follows that meaning and preserves the verse endings.
rows.anchor: لأن معنى تبتل بتل نفسه ، فجيء به على معناه مراعاة لحق الفواصل

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: Rabb al-mashriq wa-l-maghrib is read nominative as praise or genitive as apposition to rabbika.
rows.anchor: قرىء مرفوعا على المدح ، ومجرورا على البدل من ربك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the phrase as an oath with an omitted oath particle, answered by “there is no god but Him.”
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : على القسم بإضمار حرف القسم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads “Lord of the eastern places and western places.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( رب المشارق والمغارب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking God as trustee follows the declaration of His oneness: only He deserves entrusting affairs because He alone is Lord.
rows.anchor: مسبب على التهليلة ؛ لأنه هو وحده هو الذي يجب لتوحده بالربوبية أن توكل إليه الأمور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, wakīlan means a guarantor of God's promised victory and triumph.
rows.anchor: وقيل { وكيلا } : كفيلا بما وعدك من النصر والإظهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautifully forsaking them means turning away in heart and desire, while differing gently, accommodating them, overlooking, and not retaliating.
rows.anchor: أن يجانبهم بقلبه وهواه ، ويخالفهم مع حسن المخالفة والمداراة والإغضاء وترك المكافأة

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ says they smile and laugh in some people's faces though their hearts reject them.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه : إنا لنكشر في وجوه قوم ونضحك إليهم ، وإن قلوبنا لتقليهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the command to forsake them beautifully was abrogated by the sword verse.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو منسوخ بآية السيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adnā min thuluthay al-layl means less than two thirds; “nearer” is figuratively “less,” since less distance means fewer intervening spaces.
rows.anchor: أقل منهما ؛ وإنما استعير الأدنى وهو الأقرب للأقل ؛ لأن المسافة بين الشيئين إذا دنت : قل ما بينهما من الأحياز

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: The accusative reading means they stand less than two thirds, or stand half or a third, matching the earlier options of a full half, a shorter third, or more than half but less than two thirds.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ونصفه وثلثه ) بالنصب على أنك تقوم أقل من الثلثين ، وتقوم النصف والثلث : وهو مطابق لما مر في أول السورة

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: The genitive reading means less than two thirds, less than half, and less than a third; the available periods are half, a third, and a quarter.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ونصفه ) ، وثلثه : بالجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of the Prophet's companions also perform the night vigil.
rows.anchor: وطائفة من الذين معك } ويقوم ذلك جماعة من أصحابك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God can measure the night and day or know the lengths of their hours; placing God's name before “measures” emphasizes this exclusive power.
rows.anchor: ولا يقدر على تقدير الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “you cannot calculate it” refers to God's measuring; people cannot reliably track or equalize the hours, except by taking the broader, burdensome allowance.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { لن تحصوه } لمصدر يقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He relented toward you” means He licensed them to leave the prescribed night vigil, lifting the liability as from a repentant person.
rows.anchor: عبارة عن الترخيص في ترك القيام المقدر . كقوله : { فتاب عليكم وعفا عنكم فالن باشروهن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recitation names prayer by one of its pillars, as prayer is also called standing, bowing, or prostration; pray whatever night prayer is feasible. This abrogates the original command, and both are later superseded by the five prayers.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن الصلاة بالقراءة ؛ لأنها بعض أركانها ، كما عبر عنها بالقيام والركوع والسجود يريد : فصلوا ما تيسر عليكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the phrase as Qurʾān recitation itself: fifty or a hundred verses, with reports that a hundred makes one among the devout or leaves the Qurʾān unable to argue against him.
rows.anchor: قيل هي قراءة القرآن بعينها ؛ قيل : يقرأ مائة آية ومن قرأ مائة آية في ليلة لم يحاجه القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The easing is justified because night vigil is difficult for the sick, people traveling for trade, and those fighting in God's path; God thus equates fighters with travelers seeking lawful earnings.
rows.anchor: وقد بين الحكمة في النسخ . وهي تعذر القيام على المرضى ، والضاربين في الأرض للتجارة ، والمجاهدين في سبيل الله . وقيل : سوى الله بين المجاهدين والمسافرين لكسب الحلال

words: وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that one who patiently brings goods to a Muslim city seeking God's reward and sells at the day's price is counted among the martyrs before God.
rows.anchor: أيما رجل جلب شيئا إلى مدينة من مدائن المسلمين صابرا محتسبا

words: وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that, after being killed in God's path, he would prefer to die while traveling on a mount in search of God's bounty over any other death.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمر : ما خلق الله موتة أموتها بعد القتل في سبيل الله أحب إلي من أن أموت بين شعبتي رجل : أضرب في الأرض أبتغي من فضل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He knew” begins a new sentence, answering the implied question about the reason for abrogation.
rows.anchor: استئناف على تقدير السؤال عن وجه النسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer means the obligatory prayers; zakāh means the obligatory alms, or alternatively zakāt al-fiṭr, since regular zakāh had not yet been required in Mecca.
rows.anchor: يعني المفروضة والزكاة الواجبة وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If zakāh here means the obligatory alms tax, the end of the sūra is Medinan.
rows.anchor: وإنما وجبت بعد ذلك . ومن فسرها بالزكاة الواجبة جعل آخر السورة مدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Lend God a good loan” can mean voluntary charity, giving obligatory zakāh excellently and sincerely to its rightful recipients, or any good done with one's person or wealth.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يريد : سائر الصدقات وأن يريد : أداء الزكاة على أحسن وجه : من إخراج أطيب المال وأعوده على الفقراء ، ومراعاة النية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayran is the second object of wajada and a separator; this is allowed although it is not between two definite nouns because afʿal min resists the definite article.
rows.anchor: ثاني مفعولي وجد . وهو فصل . وجاز وإن لم يقع بين معرفتين . لأن أفعل من أشبه في امتناعه من حرف التعريف المعرفة

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abū al-Sammāl reads “huwa khayrun wa-aʿẓamu ajran” in the nominative, with a nominal subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال ( هو خير وأعظم أجرا ) بالرفع على الابتداء والخبر

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says whoever recites Sūrat al-Muzzammil will be spared hardship in this world and the next; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
